answer: One defence is behaviour-based reputation that decays over time. A new agent starts with almost no trust and must earn it through a long history of honest, useful work, like a wharf that only grants berths to ships with a proven record. Trust is not transferable, it fades without continued good conduct, and one abuse wipes out months of standing. An attacker must run many fake identities for months before they matter, while a sudden gale of lookalike new accounts is easy to spot and quarantine. Such a reputation, polished like an opal, costs time, which makes mass Sybil creation uneconomical.
